questions.question_text: Find the sum of the first $16$ terms of an arithmetic progression with $a = 7$ and $d = 3$.

options.why: Used $nd = 16(3) = 48$ inside the formula instead of $(n - 1)d = 15(3) = 45$.
Divided the correct sum $472$ by an extra factor of $2$.
Added $14+45$ incorrectly as $58$, giving $8(58)=464$.

questions.question_text: Find the sum of the first $11$ terms of the arithmetic series $-9-4+1+\dots$.

options.why: Omitted the division by $2$, giving $11[-18+10(5)]=352$.
Omitted $2a$, giving $\frac{11}{2}[10(5)]=275$.
Reversed the sign of the bracket from $32$ to $-32$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the sum of the arithmetic series $12 + 19 + 26 + \dots + 89$.

options.why: Used $n = 11$ terms instead of the correct $n = 12$.
Used $n = 13$ terms instead of solving $89 = 12 + 7(n - 1)$.
Forgot to divide by $2$ in the partial sum formula.
Used $1+58=58$ instead of $59$, giving $10(58)=580$.
Added the first and last terms incorrectly as $61$ instead of $59$.

questions.question_text: Which expression gives the sum of the first $n$ terms of $6 + 11 + 16 + \dots$?

options.why: Used $nd$ instead of $(n-1)d$, giving $\frac n2(12+5n)$.
Gave the $n$th term formula $a_n$ rather than the series sum $S_n$.
Subtracted $7$ instead of adding $12 - 5 = +7$.

questions.question_text:
The sum of the first $10$ terms of an arithmetic progression is $175$, and the first term is $4$.
Find the common difference $d$.

options.why: Divided by $10$ instead of $9$ when solving $9d = 27$.
Divided $35$ by $10$, omitting the subtraction of $8$ and using $n$ instead of $n-1$.
Assumed $d = a$ without solving the equation.

questions.question_text: Find the sum of the first $15$ terms of the sequence $30, 25, 20, 15, \dots$.

options.why: Changed the sign to positive ignoring that the later negative terms dominate.
Forgot to divide by $2$ in the formula.
Assumed terms cancel out completely over $15$ terms.

questions.question_text:
The sum of the first $4$ terms of an AP is $40$, and the sum of the first $8$ terms is $144$.
Find the sum of the first three terms.

options.why: Reported the given sum of four terms instead of calculating the sum of three terms.
Treated all three terms as the third term, giving $3a_3=3(12)=36$.
Reported the third term $a_3=4+2(4)=12$ instead of the sum of the first three terms.

questions.question_text:
The sixth term of an AP is $24$ and the sum of its first $10$ terms is $220$.
Find the sum of its first $15$ terms.

options.why: Reported the sum of the first and fifteenth terms, $4+60=64$, without multiplying by $15/2$.
Used $15d$ instead of $14d$, giving $\frac{15}{2}[8+15(4)]=510$.
Omitted the division by $2$, giving $15[8+14(4)]=960$.

questions.question_text: An arithmetic series has $20$ terms, first term $-6$ and sum $350$. Find the last term.

options.why: Subtracted $6$ from $35$ instead of adding it when solving $35=-6+l$.
Reported $a+l=35$ without subtracting the first term $-6$.
Used $20$ instead of $20/2$, giving $350=20(-6+l)$ and $l=23.5$.
